source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) belongs to the group of fruit-type crops grown for both fresh fruit consumption and as a vegetable-like crop in home gardens. It is grown across many countries, and while it is not a staple food, it is very widely consumed as a fresh fruit worldwide.

A nutritional composition table for watermelon flesh (per 100 g edible portion) lists: water content approximately 55 g, sugars 3.3 g, cellulose/fiber 0.2 g, protein 0.2 g, vitamin B 0.04 mg, vitamin C 9 mg, calcium 11 mg, and iron 7.9 mg (figures as printed in the source table; some values are hard to read with full precision due to table alignment in the scanned original and should be treated as approximate).

Selection of good quality seed is very important. Seed should be sourced with knowledge of its harvest date, month, and year of production, its purity, and its germination rate, ideally from seed that has been officially recommended for use. Hybrid F1 seed cannot be saved and reused from a previous harvest because it is produced by seed companies through controlled crossing; farmers are advised to purchase fresh hybrid seed for each planting rather than retaining seed from their own hybrid fruit.
